name: Final Fantasy
strap: Choose a world. You do not need the whole series.
intro: Final Fantasy is a family of worlds, not one story running from I to XVI. Familiar creatures, magic and names invite recognition, while most numbered games introduce new people and histories. Pick the kind of journey you want, then follow that world’s relationships and conflicts.
recommendation: Start X for a clear, turn-based journey into an unfamiliar culture, IX for storybook fantasy with thoughtful characters, or XVI for action and a darker political world. VI is an excellent pixel-era choice. VII Remake begins a connected modern project; it is not a replacement that contains the entire 1997 story.
description: Where to start Final Fantasy, which stories connect, and the lore, motives and relationships worth knowing.
basics: The number usually marks a new world

X is not a sequel to IX. A suffix often signals a direct continuation: X-2 follows X, and XIII-2 follows XIII. The VII remake project is a connected sequence within VII’s world. Those local connections matter more than the franchise number.

Crystals, summons, chocobos, moogles and people named Cid recur. Their identities and functions change by game. A Cid in one world does not normally carry another Cid’s biography, and a familiar summon need not have the same origin.
Choose a play style as well as a story

Combat ranges from command-based parties to real-time action and online role-playing. XI and XIV are separate online games; neither requires the other. Early North American releases called IV “II” and VI “III”; this guide uses the original Japanese numbering to avoid that confusion.

entries.title: Final Fantasy X
entries.audience: I want turn-based combat and a clear story
entries.why: Tidus enters Spira as an outsider, so the world explains itself alongside him. The pilgrimage gives you a focused route through people, places and beliefs.
entries.need: Sin threatens Spira. Yuna is a summoner undertaking a pilgrimage, and Tidus becomes one of her companions.
entries.skip: I–IX, every optional boss, and X-2 until you want to stay in this world.
entries.tradeoff: Its linear journey and deliberate battles differ from open-world RPGs. Some optional challenges are far more demanding than the main story.
entries.next: Choose X-2 only after X if you want more of Yuna and Spira. It changes tone and combat; you can finish X and stop.

entries.title: Final Fantasy IX
entries.audience: I want warm fantasy with serious questions
entries.why: A theatre troupe, a princess and a young mage offer an inviting opening. Their worries about identity, belonging and duty grow out of the adventure rather than a lore lecture.
entries.need: Zidane’s troupe visits Alexandria, where Garnet’s concerns and Vivi’s unexpected involvement bring them together.
entries.skip: Every other Final Fantasy, a glossary of recurring monsters, and optional completion challenges.
entries.tradeoff: Its older battle pace and presentation may require adjustment. The playful look does not mean every part of the story is lighthearted.
entries.next: VI offers another ensemble story about power and identity; X offers a more directed pilgrimage. Neither is a continuation you must play.

entries.title: Final Fantasy VII Remake
entries.audience: I want a modern cast and action with tactical choices
entries.why: Midgar gives Cloud’s party a strong local beginning. Their competing motives make the conflict with Shinra understandable before the larger mysteries widen.
entries.need: Cloud accepts work with Avalanche, a group opposing a company that draws energy from the planet.
entries.skip: I–VI, the 1997 game before beginning, Crisis Core as compulsory homework, and the films or mobile games.
entries.tradeoff: This is the first part of a connected reimagining, not the entire original VII. Familiar material develops differently; first-time players may find some late mysteries deliberately unresolved.
entries.next: Continue Rebirth. Intergrade is an expanded edition of Remake, and its INTERmission episode is an optional Yuffie detour before Rebirth. The project’s final announced chapter is future orientation here. Choose original VII instead if you want the complete original story in one game.

entries.title: Final Fantasy VI, including Pixel Remaster
entries.audience: I want the pixel-era ensemble and its lore
entries.why: Different people reveal different costs of imperial power. A relatively compact visual style makes its towns, character scenes and escalating conflict easy to read.
entries.need: An empire turns rediscovered magic into military power. Terra’s place in that system is the opening question.
entries.skip: I–V, buying the whole Pixel Remaster collection, and finding every secret before advancing.
entries.tradeoff: It uses older navigation and timed command battles. There is no single protagonist whose route substitutes for the whole ensemble.
entries.next: Try IV for a more focused redemption story, or IX for another cast wrestling with belonging. Each begins afresh.

entries.title: Final Fantasy XVI
entries.audience: I want action combat and a darker political story
entries.why: Clive’s family bonds and the treatment of people with magic give its wars concrete human stakes. The game introduces its own vocabulary and nations.
entries.need: Valisthea’s nations depend on powerful crystals. Certain people wield Eikons, while others are exploited for magical ability.
entries.skip: All earlier Final Fantasy games, understanding every summon before playing, and the expansions before the base adventure.
entries.tradeoff: It focuses on one directly controlled fighter rather than turn-based party management. Violence and adult themes make it a different tone from IX.
entries.next: Echoes of the Fallen and The Rising Tide are optional additions with late-game requirements. XV offers a separate action-oriented road trip with a stronger traveling-party emphasis.

entries.title: Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn
entries.audience: I want a long story in an online world
entries.why: Your own adventurer grows into a central role while recurring allies give an expanding world continuity. Start with the main scenario rather than treating years of updates as an immediate obligation.
entries.need: Begin as an adventurer in Eorzea. Main Scenario Quests introduce the institutions, companions and conflicts you need.
entries.skip: I–XIII, the retired original XIV release, XI, raids and other optional activities until they interest you.
entries.tradeoff: It is a substantial online commitment with multiplayer elements. Account, trial and subscription conditions vary; check the official options before choosing an edition.
entries.next: Continue the main scenario through Heavensward → Stormblood → Shadowbringers → Endwalker → Dawntrail as your interest grows. Finishing a chapter is a reasonable stopping point; the guide does not require catching up to every patch.

events.title: Final Fantasy
events.premise: Four travelers bearing crystals begin a quest to restore the elements.
events.why: Optional original, available in Pixel Remaster. Its sparse character writing differs from later ensemble stories.

events.title: Final Fantasy II
events.premise: Survivors join a rebellion against Palamecia’s conquest.
events.why: A separate world, not the first game’s next chapter. Its progression system differs from conventional level growth.

events.title: Final Fantasy III
events.premise: Chosen adventurers take up a crystal-linked mission as darkness grows.
events.why: Independent job-system adventure. The original-style Pixel Remaster and 3D remake use different presentations and casts.

events.title: Final Fantasy IV
events.premise: Cecil’s service to Baron becomes a conflict between obedience and conscience.
events.why: A focused classic alternative. Pixel Remaster and the 3D remake differ in systems; The After Years is an optional later continuation.

events.title: Final Fantasy V
events.premise: A crisis around the crystals brings a small group together.
events.why: Independent adventure suited to experimenting with party jobs. It does not supply the background needed for VI.

events.title: Final Fantasy VI
events.premise: Terra and an expanding ensemble confront the use of magic as a weapon.
events.why: Recommended pixel-era starting point. The original and Pixel Remaster tell the same central story.
events.recap: The party defeats Kefka; magic fades from the world, while Terra survives and the companions look toward rebuilding.

events.title: Final Fantasy VII
events.premise: Cloud joins an anti-Shinra group as a local fight opens into a larger danger.
events.why: Complete original adventure. Play this before Crisis Core if you want to discover its central mysteries in their original order.
events.recap: The party defeats Sephiroth, and the Lifestream helps counter Meteor’s threat to the planet.

events.title: Final Fantasy Tactics
events.premise: Ramza and Delita face political conflict from unequal places within the same society.
events.why: Optional tactical beginning, including The Ivalice Chronicles edition. It shares the Ivalice name with XII, but this guide does not turn them into a required two-game sequence.

events.title: Final Fantasy VIII
events.premise: A young mercenary unit becomes entangled in a conflict involving sorceresses.
events.why: Independent world with a junction-based combat system; VII’s story is unnecessary.

events.title: Final Fantasy IX
events.premise: An encounter brings Zidane, Garnet and Vivi into a journey shaped by war and questions about their past.
events.why: Recommended storybook-fantasy beginning. Recurring motifs are recognition bonuses, not hidden prerequisites.
events.recap: Zidane returns and reunites with Garnet after the party’s confrontation with Kuja and the threat beyond him.

events.title: Final Fantasy X
events.premise: Tidus travels with Yuna and her guardians across a world living under Sin’s threat.
events.why: Recommended turn-based beginning. X-2 is the direct follow-up; XI is a different world.
events.recap: Yuna and her guardians defeat Yu Yevon and break Sin’s cycle. Tidus fades as the dream sustaining his existence ends.

events.title: Final Fantasy XI
events.premise: A player-created adventurer joins Vana’diel’s nations and wider conflicts.
events.why: Separate online world. This first guide is orientation only, not a full expansion or mission chronicle; check official service and account details.

events.title: Final Fantasy X-2
events.premise: Yuna, Rikku and Paine follow a new adventure two years after X.
events.why: Direct sequel; play after X. It introduces a different structure and job-based combat, rather than beginning XII’s world.

events.title: Final Fantasy XII
events.premise: An occupied kingdom’s people become entangled with royalty, sky pirates and imperial ambition.
events.why: Independent political adventure. The Zodiac Age revises its systems; Tactics is not required.

events.title: Crisis Core: Final Fantasy VII
events.premise: Zack’s SOLDIER assignments expose troubling questions about Shinra’s work.
events.why: Optional prequel, also told by Reunion. Earlier setting does not make it our first-play recommendation: it reveals background that original VII treats as mystery.

events.title: Final Fantasy XIII
events.premise: Lightning and other fugitives are forced into a mission by powerful beings.
events.why: A new numbered world. XIII-2 and Lightning Returns continue it; neither should be mistaken for XIV.

events.title: Final Fantasy XIII-2
events.premise: Serah and Noel search across time for answers about Lightning and a threatened future.
events.why: Best after XIII. Time travel is internal to this world, not a bridge through every numbered game.

events.title: Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
events.premise: Lightning takes on a new task as this world approaches a reckoning.
events.why: Concludes the XIII sequence. Its time-management and solo combat structure differ from the first two games.

events.title: Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn
events.premise: Your adventurer enters Eorzea and becomes involved in its growing conflicts.
events.why: Recommended online entry. The 2010 release is retired; begin A Realm Reborn and follow its main scenario, not a missing older campaign.

events.title: Final Fantasy XV
events.era: A prince and his traveling companions
events.premise: Noctis leaves home with three friends as an imperial conflict changes their plans.
events.why: Independent action RPG. Royal and Windows editions expand the base experience; DLC and companion media provide optional context.

events.title: Final Fantasy VII Remake
events.premise: Cloud’s work with Avalanche grows into a struggle for the city and the planet.
events.why: Recommended modern VII beginning. Intergrade is an edition of this chapter; Rebirth is its next game.

events.title: Final Fantasy XVI
events.premise: Clive’s life is shaped by family loss and a society built around magical power.
events.why: Recommended action beginning. This world explains its own nations and terminology.
events.recap: Clive defeats Ultima and acts to end the system of magic that has bound Valisthea. The ending leaves individual survival open to interpretation.

events.title: Final Fantasy VII Rebirth
events.premise: Cloud’s companions travel beyond the city while their search and relationships widen.
events.why: Second chapter of the remake project; play after Remake. Neither game alone contains the original VII’s complete plot.

events.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation
events.premise: A final chapter of the VII remake project has been announced.
events.why: Future orientation only; no outcome recap or completed-release claim. This guide does not transfer the 1997 ending onto a new telling.

characters.name: Cecil Harvey
characters.motivation: Cecil’s defining question is whether loyalty excuses the orders he carries out. His relationships make conscience more than an abstract ideal.
characters.relationships: Rosa and Kain belong to his own world. Their history begins within IV rather than the first three games.

characters.name: Terra Branford
characters.motivation: Terra wants a life beyond being used as a weapon. Her search for belonging gives the empire’s treatment of magic a human face.
characters.relationships: The Returners offer a possible place for her; the ensemble lets other lives challenge and widen the same conflict.

characters.name: Celes Chere
characters.motivation: Celes questions the power she has served. Her struggle is about the possibility of choosing a different responsibility after being shaped by an empire.
characters.relationships: An imperial general who crosses paths with the resistance and Terra’s companions.

characters.name: Cloud Strife
characters.motivation: Cloud initially presents himself as a skilled professional. The people around him gradually test the distance between that pose and his actual commitments.
characters.relationships: Tifa knows his earlier life; Aerith and Barret challenge different parts of his outlook. Original VII and the remake project revisit these connections differently.

characters.name: Tifa Lockhart
characters.motivation: Tifa’s care for people gives the fight against Shinra a local home. Her connection to Cloud carries questions that should be discovered inside the story.
characters.relationships: Cloud’s childhood friend and an Avalanche member, balancing private concerns with a wider struggle.

characters.name: Aerith Gainsborough
characters.role: VII / an ordinary life under pressure
characters.motivation: Aerith’s warmth sits beside a determination to choose her own life. Shinra’s interest in her turns a personal wish into a question of power and purpose.
characters.relationships: Her friendship with Cloud’s party introduces new perspectives on the planet; Crisis Core supplies optional earlier context.

characters.name: Barret Wallace
characters.motivation: Barret’s anger at Shinra is tied to both the planet and the people he loves. His responsibility for Marlene keeps resistance grounded in a future worth protecting.
characters.relationships: An Avalanche leader and Marlene’s adoptive father; the same core relationship anchors different tellings.

characters.name: Zack Fair
characters.motivation: Zack wants to live up to the heroic image of SOLDIER. His assignments make that ambition collide with what the institution actually does.
characters.relationships: Crisis Core follows him; Cloud and Aerith connect his life to VII. Save the prequel for later if you want original VII’s mysteries preserved.

characters.name: Zidane Tribal
characters.motivation: Zidane’s readiness to help strangers turns an apparently light adventure into a search for belonging. His history is a question the game earns time to answer.
characters.relationships: A member of Tantalus whose journey brings him alongside Garnet and Vivi.

characters.name: Vivi Ornitier
characters.role: IX / a young mage asking who he is
characters.motivation: Vivi’s uncertainty gives large questions about existence a small, recognizable voice. His friendships matter because he is learning how to live, not merely where his powers came from.
characters.relationships: An accidental participant in the opening events who becomes part of Zidane’s traveling group.

characters.name: Tidus
characters.motivation: Tidus wants a way home and answers about his father. His unfamiliarity with Spira lets him ask questions its people have learned to accept.
characters.relationships: Yuna’s guardian; Auron and the other companions connect personal history with the pilgrimage.

updates.text: His existence ends with the dream behind it, making the journey’s farewell personal.

characters.name: Yuna
characters.role: X / duty and the life beyond it
characters.motivation: Yuna’s concern for other people makes the pilgrimage a commitment, not an abstract religious task. Watch how her own voice develops alongside the duties assigned to her.
characters.relationships: Tidus and her guardians support her in X. Rikku and Paine join her later X-2 journey, which is optional after X.

updates.text: She rejects the inherited cycle and helps find a way to defeat Sin permanently.

characters.name: Ashelia “Ashe” B’nargin Dalmasca
characters.motivation: Ashe’s responsibility to a conquered kingdom competes with the personal force of grief. Her choices make the question of restoring power more complicated than recovering a throne.
characters.relationships: Vaan and the sky pirates encounter a royal struggle through different social positions.

characters.name: Lightning
characters.role: XIII / a sister and an imposed fate
characters.motivation: Lightning’s protective instincts drive her into conflict with institutions that dictate what people must become. Her trilogy changes protagonists and systems while continuing the same family’s story.
characters.relationships: Serah is her sister. XIII-2 follows Serah and Noel; Lightning returns to the lead in the concluding game.

characters.name: Your adventurer / Warrior of Light
characters.motivation: The online story gives your chosen adventurer growing responsibilities and continuing relationships. The point is a life in this world, not replacing another numbered protagonist.
characters.relationships: Eorzea’s companions and institutions are introduced through the main scenario. This profile avoids later identities and expansion outcomes.

characters.name: Noctis Lucis Caelum
characters.motivation: Noctis’s royal obligations are felt through a journey with friends who know the person beneath the title. Their everyday routines make the larger conflict intimate.
characters.relationships: Gladiolus protects him, Ignis cares for the group, and Prompto brings a friend’s perspective beyond royal service.

characters.name: Clive Rosfield
characters.motivation: Clive begins by seeking a role that protects his younger brother. Family loss and the treatment of people with magic push his responsibilities beyond that first identity.
characters.relationships: Joshua, Jill and Cid make the political struggle personal. This Cid is a person of Valisthea, not VII’s pilot continuing his life.

updates.text: His final action rejects Ultima’s use of human lives; the aftermath does not settle every person’s fate unambiguously.

characters.name: Jill Warrick
characters.motivation: Jill’s history with the Rosfield family gives her relationship with Clive roots before the wider conflict. Her own experience of power and obligation deserves attention alongside his.
characters.relationships: Raised with Clive and Joshua, later associated with Shiva’s power.

characters.name: Ramza Beoulve
characters.motivation: Ramza’s position within a military family is tested by the people that social order excludes. His friendship with Delita makes class and ambition part of a personal story.
characters.relationships: Delita grew up alongside him from a different social background. XII’s cast is unnecessary to understand their conflict.

factions: VII: Shinra, Avalanche and the planet

Shinra’s energy monopoly connects comfort and prosperity to extracting the planet’s life. Avalanche resists it, but individual members’ motives differ. That tension explains the opening without needing the whole Compilation of VII.
X: belief, Sin and the pilgrimage

Yevon’s teachings shape how Spira understands recurring disaster. Yuna’s guardians and the people they meet reveal what that belief costs and what it sustains. Let the pilgrimage disclose the deeper truths rather than beginning with an ending summary.

The empire seeks to turn magical beings and people into instruments of conquest. The resistance gathers different lives affected by that project. Terra and Celes show that being made useful to power is not the same as choosing a purpose.

Mothercrystals underpin national power. Bearers are exploited for magic, while Dominants’ Eikons make them strategic assets. The distinctions matter because the same society assigns radically different value to different people’s abilities.

XII and Tactics each make war, institutions and unequal status central to their own casts. Shared names and setting associations enrich comparison; this guide gives each a separate route and makes no claim that one is required background for the other.
XI and XIV: separate online worlds

Vana’diel and Eorzea are different commitments. Begin the chosen game’s introductory missions or main scenario, then follow its own expansions. This guide introduces the worlds rather than summarizing years of online story outcomes.

milestones.label: Reveal all published outcomes in this guide

atlas_intro: Each card opens a smaller set of connected stories. These are independent worlds, not three strands of one history. Use the world filter for the other numbered games.

strands.name: X / Spira
strands.title: A pilgrimage and its people
strands.text: Tidus discovers Spira alongside you. Yuna’s commitments and her guardians make the world’s beliefs personal.

strands.name: VII / Remake project
strands.title: A city, a company and a planet
strands.text: Begin with Remake, then Rebirth. Follow Cloud’s party through this new telling without first playing I–VI.

strands.name: XVI / Valisthea
strands.title: Power carried by human beings
strands.text: Clive’s story explores a society that turns magical ability into status, obligation and exploitation. No earlier numbered game is required.

timeline_help: Release years use first original releases, usually in Japan; editions may have later dates. “Group connected stories” places each world together and orders its included connections. It does not create a chronology from I to XVI. Crisis Core is earlier within original VII’s world but is recommended later for first-time mystery preservation. The remake project has a separate group and spoiler boundary. The starting-route filter shows alternative beginnings and Remake’s direct released follow-up, not a compulsory sequence across worlds.
scope: A first lore atlas for all sixteen numbered entries, with selected connected games: X-2, XIII-2, Lightning Returns, Crisis Core, VII Remake and Rebirth, plus Tactics and the announced VII Revelation. MMO entries are introductory only: XI’s expansions and XIV’s ongoing patches are not exhaustively summarized. XIV’s original 2010 service is distinguished from the 2013 A Realm Reborn entry point. Pixel Remaster, Zodiac Age, Intergrade, Reunion and The Ivalice Chronicles are editions or retellings of indexed stories, not additional mandatory sequels. IV: The After Years, XII: Revenant Wings, other spin-offs, VII’s films and mobile games, XV’s companion media and selected DLC are optional deeper material outside this timeline’s full coverage. Published recaps are selected endings, not comprehensive plot summaries. No announced game’s ending is assumed from an older telling.
